# Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec
Feature: wfx-erp-product-sales · Owner: Vinod Khanna (Technical Architect)
Functional specification for the development team, generated from the finished, product-team-approved Product Mock Studio screens (feature library wfx-erp-product-sales). This document contains ASSUMED answers pending product-team sign-off (see Section 8).

## Overview
This document specifies the Sales Orders feature for the real WFX ERP application. It was generated from the finished, product-team-approved mock screens in the Product Mock Studio (feature library wfx-erp-product-sales). The mock is intentionally lenient; this specification is not — it is the contract the development team builds from, and it goes to QA and then to live production.

### Purpose
Sales Orders (order confirmations, “OC”) are the commercial head record of the ERP: one order belongs to one buyer, carries a season, currency, manager, total quantity and value, key dates, and free-text fabric/packing instructions. The feature lets the sales/merchandising team create, search, review, confirm, cancel and (within strict rules) delete sales orders.

### Who uses it2
• Merchandisers / sales coordinators — create and maintain orders, enter instructions.
• Sales managers — review and Confirm orders, cancel with a reason.
• Downstream teams (planning, production, shipping) — read confirmed order data; they do not edit here.

### Where it sits in the ERP
The feature lives in the Sales module (real target: libs/angular/features/wfx-erp/wfx-erp-sales, route /sales). It is the upstream source for production planning, BOM and shipment documents; statuses beyond Confirmed (Part Ship, Shipped, Closed) are driven by those downstream modules, not by these two screens.
Scope of this spec: the Sales Order LIST screen and the Sales Order DETAIL (create/edit) screen, including their shared workflow, data contract, and validations. Order line items (article / size / colourway breakdowns) are not part of the mock and are out of scope (see Section 7).

## Screen inventory & navigation flow

[TABLE 1: Table 1 · 3 rows · columns: # (text), Screen (text), Route (text), Purpose (text)]
| # | Screen | Route | Purpose |
| S-1 | Sales Order List | /sales/orders | Search, filter, and manage all sales orders; entry point of the feature. /sales redirects here. |
| S-2 | Sales Order Detail — New | /sales/orders/new | Create a new order. The record is inserted automatically once all seed fields are filled (auto-save; no Save button). |
| S-3 | Sales Order Detail — Edit | /sales/orders/{id} | View and edit an existing order; manual Confirm action. |

### Navigation rules
• List → Detail (edit): click the order-number link in the Order column, or right-click a row and choose Edit. Both open /sales/orders/{id}.
• List → Detail (new): the “+ Add New Order” button in the page toolbar opens /sales/orders/new.
• Detail → List: the back arrow in the page header returns to /sales/orders. Any pending auto-save is flushed before navigating away; the flush must complete (or fail with an error toast) — a navigation must never silently drop an unsaved change.
• Unknown order id: an error toast “That sales order does not exist.” is shown and the user is returned to the list.
• Browser/page titles: “Sales Orders” (list), “New Sales Order” (new), “Sales Order” (edit).
Back-navigation state: the mock does not preserve list state (filters, page) across detail visits. The real screen must restore the list exactly as the user left it — search text, status filter, column filters, sort and page (QA checklist §5). See Q-17/Q-18 in Section 8.

## Conventions
Rules referenced throughout the field tables and the Validations master list are defined once here, so no field restates them.

[TABLE 2: Table 2 · 5 rows · columns: Convention (text), Definition (text) · identifiers: Convention]
| Convention | Definition |
| Enforcement | Unless a rule says otherwise, every validation is enforced inline on the Detail form and re-validated on the server. |
| Seed fields | Ship Under PO Ref, Buyer, Category, Currency, Total Quantity, Total Value. A new order is auto-created only once all seed fields are filled and valid (V-14). |
| Text fields | Trimmed; a mandatory text field must contain at least one non-whitespace character; length hard-stops at the stated maximum. |
| Money | ≥ 0, at most 2 decimal places, displayed with exactly 2 decimals and the order’s currency. |
| Date display | All dates display via the app-wide WfxDateFormatService (user preference, default dd MMM yyyy) — never a hardcoded locale. |

## Screen specifications

### Sales Order List (S-1)
Purpose: single working list of all sales orders with search, filters, bulk selection, row actions and navigation into the detail screen.
Sales Order List — light mode, Team Data

#### Layout
• Page header: breadcrumb “Sales”, title “Sales Orders”, subtitle, and a primary “+ Add New Order” button.
• Content toolbar: quick-search input (“Search by order no. or buyer”) and a clearable, searchable Status dropdown.
• Grid inside a surface card; floating filter row pinned under the headers; pagination footer always visible (never covered by other UI).
• Floating selection bar appears when one or more rows are selected, with the selection count, a Clear action, and a Delete action.

#### Toolbar behaviours
• Quick search matches Order No (MainOCNum) OR Buyer name, case-insensitive substring, trimmed. Real build: debounce 300 ms and extend to PO Ref (ASSUMED — Q-17).
• Status dropdown filters to exactly one status; clearable (shows all). Values: Saved, Confirmed, Part Ship, Shipped, Closed, Cancelled.
• Toolbar filters and in-grid column filters combine (logical AND).

#### Grid specification

[TABLE 3: Table 3 · 12 rows · columns: Column (text), Content & combined cells (text), Filter (text), Format / behaviour (text) · identifiers: Column]
| Column | Content & combined cells | Filter | Format / behaviour |
| (selection) | Row checkbox + header checkbox | — | Multi-row selection; header checkbox selects the filtered set only. |
| Status | wfx-badge chip, never plain text | Set filter (checkbox list of the 6 statuses, fixed order) | Severity: Saved=draft, Confirmed=success, Shipped=success, Part Ship=warning, Cancelled=error. Closed: see Q-21. |
| Order | Combined cell — Order No (link, opens detail) over Ship Under PO Ref (secondary line) | Text filter | Link handled via data-action="open-order" + onCellClicked; autoHeight on. |
| Buyer | Combined cell — Buyer name over buyer code | Set filter | autoHeight on. |
| Category | Product category code | Set filter | — |
| Season | Season code | Set filter | — |
| Manager | Manager name | Set filter | Avatar (initials) + name — every person-valued column renders the shared user renderer, never a bare string. |
| Total Qty | Order quantity | Number filter | Right-aligned, thousand separators, WITH its UOM (ASSUMED “pcs” — Q-1). Mock omits the UOM — flagged, Section 7.2. |
| Total Value | Order value | Number filter | Right-aligned; currency symbol + code of the record’s CurrencyCode; 2 decimals everywhere (ASSUMED — Q-2). Number locale is still hardcoded en-US in the mock — flagged, Section 7.2. |
| Delivery Date | Delivery date | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | App-wide date format via WfxDateFormatService (user preference, default dd MMM yyyy). Calendar picker; a from–to range includes both endpoint days. |
| Created By | Who created the order | Set filter | Avatar (initials) + name. A SEPARATE column from Created On — never merged into one “Created” cell — and it precedes Created On in every list. autoHeight on. |
| Created On | Creation date | Date (equals / before / after / from–to) | Same date rules as Delivery Date. |
• Default column config: resizable, sortable, floating filter row on, min width 90.
• Set-filter values: fed from the DDL API in the real app (mock auto-derives from row data).
• Pagination: page sizes 20 / 50 / 100, default 20. Default sort: Created On descending (ASSUMED — Q-18).
• Row model: the mock grid is client-side. The real screen must use the server-side row model with server paging, sorting and filtering from day one (ASSUMED — Q-18); see Section 7.1.
• Actions column: the mock exposes row actions only through the right-click context menu. The real screen must additionally provide a pinned-right actions column (kebab) with the same items, per grid standards — right-click alone is not discoverable. Flagged in Section 7.2.

#### Row actions (context menu)
Row context menu on a Saved order (Practice Copy)

[TABLE 4: Table 4 · 4 rows · columns: Action (text), Shown when (text), Behaviour (text) · identifiers: Action]
| Action | Shown when | Behaviour |
| Edit | Always | Opens the detail screen for the row. |
| Confirm | Status = Saved | Confirmation dialog, then sets Status = Confirmed (see Section 4). |
| Cancel | Status is not Cancelled and not Closed (real rule: Saved or Confirmed only — ASSUMED, Q-12) | Opens the Cancel Order dialog; reason is mandatory. |
| Delete | Status = Saved or Cancelled in the mock (real rule: Saved only — ASSUMED, Q-15) | Confirmation dialog, then hard delete. |

#### Bulk actions
• Selecting rows shows the floating selection bar with the count and a Delete button.
• Bulk delete first validates every selected row against the delete rule; if any row is not deletable the whole action is blocked with a warning naming the blocked orders — nothing is partially deleted.
• After a successful bulk delete the selection is cleared and the list reloads.

#### Cancel Order dialog
Cancel Order dialog — reason is mandatory
• Modal, header “Cancel Order”, helper text “Enter a reason to cancel this order.”, one required Reason textarea (4 rows), buttons OK (primary) / Close.
• OK with a blank/whitespace reason shows the warning “Reason is mandatory.” and keeps the dialog open.
• OK with a reason sets Status = Cancelled and stores the reason. The real build stores it in a dedicated CancelReason field with an audit entry (who/when); it must NOT overwrite the order’s Comments as the mock does — flagged, Section 7.2 (ASSUMED — Q-13).
• Close / X dismisses without changes.
• Real build addition: the dialog must name the order being cancelled (e.g. “Cancel OC-2026-0001”) — the mock text is generic.

#### Empty, loading and error states
• Empty list: grid shows its no-rows overlay. Real build: message “No sales orders found” with an Add New Order call to action (ASSUMED — Q-22).
• Load failure: error toast “Load Failed — Could not load sales orders.” with retry guidance; the grid stays empty, never silently blank.

### Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3)
Purpose: create and edit a sales order. There is NO Save button — the screen auto-saves (see 3.2.3). Confirm is the only manual action.
Detail — Info tab (existing order, Team Data)
Detail — Instruction tab
Detail — Add Sales Order (empty form, Practice Copy)

#### Layout
• Page header: breadcrumbs “Sales › Sales Orders”, back arrow, title “Add Sales Order” (new) or “Sales Order {MainOCNum}” (existing), save-status indicator, and the Confirm button (visible once the record exists).
• Two tabs: Info (Order Information panel, responsive form grid, min field width 220px) and Instruction (three toggleable panels: Fabric Instruction, Packing Instruction, Comments & Notes).

#### Field table — Info tab

[TABLE 5: Table 5 · 10 rows · columns: Field (text), Type (text), Required (text), Validation (text), Default (text), Source / DDL (text) · identifiers: Field]
| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Default | Source / DDL |
| Ship Under PO Ref | Text input | Yes (seed) | V-1 (max 100, not blank) | empty | Free text; uniqueness per buyer ASSUMED — Q-6 |
| Buyer | Select (searchable) | Yes (seed) | V-2 | none | Buyer DDL API (mock: 3 static buyers) |
| Category | Select | Yes (seed) | V-3 | none | Product category DDL (mock: Apparel, Knits, Woven, Denim) |
| Order Season | Select (clearable) | No | — | none | Season DDL (mock: SS26, AW26, SS27); optional ASSUMED — Q-10 |
| Currency | Select | Yes (seed) | V-4 | none | Currency DDL (mock: USD, EUR, GBP, INR) |
| Manager | Text input | No | V-5 (max 100) | empty | Mock: free text. Real: user DDL — ASSUMED, Q-11 |
| Total Quantity | Number input | Yes (seed) | V-6 (integer 1–1,000,000) | empty | — (display with UOM, Q-1) |
| Total Value | Number input | Yes (seed) | V-7 (0–99,999,999; 2 dp) | empty | — (currency per order) |
| Order Initiation Date | Date picker | No (see Q-8) | Cross-field V-8 | empty | App-wide date format |
| Delivery Date | Date picker | No (see Q-8) | V-8 (≥ Order Initiation Date) | empty | App-wide date format |

#### Field table — Instruction tab

[TABLE 6: Table 6 · 3 rows · columns: Field (text), Type (text), Required (boolean), Validation (text), Default (text), Notes (text)]
| Field | Type | Required | Validation | Default | Notes |
| Fabric Instruction | Textarea (5 rows) | No | V-9 (max 1000) | empty | Placeholder: “Enter fabric composition, GSM, finish...” |
| Packing Instruction | Textarea (5 rows) | No | V-10 (max 1000) | empty | Placeholder: “Enter carton ratio, polybag, labelling...” |
| Comments | Textarea (4 rows) | No | Max length TBD — Q-13a | empty | Internal notes. Must never be overwritten by the cancel reason (Section 7.2). |

#### Auto-save behaviour
• Seed fields (all must be filled before the record is created): Ship Under PO Ref, Buyer, Category, Currency, Total Quantity, Total Value. Season, dates and all Instruction-tab fields are NOT seed fields.
• New order: the record is inserted automatically the moment the last seed field is filled and valid. The server assigns the real order number at this insert (ASSUMED — Q-7); the mock’s client-side “OC-DRAFT-nnnnnn” placeholder must not ship.
• Existing order: every change is debounce-saved automatically. The mock PUTs the whole record; the real screen PATCHes only the dirty fields (Section 7.1).
• The save-status indicator in the toolbar shows idle → saving → saved / error. A failed save shows the toast “Save Failed — Could not save the sales order.” and the indicator stays in the error state until a subsequent save succeeds.
• Navigating back flushes any pending save first (see Section 2).
• Loaded values never count as dirty — opening an order must not trigger a save.

#### Validation display
Empty required (seed) fields highlighted after being touched
• Errors appear inline per field once the field is touched, using the standard field-error styling; required fields carry the * marker.
• Exact rule texts are in Section 6 (Validations master list).

#### Confirm action
Confirm dialog (first confirmation)
• Confirm is visible for any existing (already auto-saved) record — including an already-Confirmed one. Re-confirm after an edit is deliberate: in the real app, editing a confirmed order creates a new background version in Saved status, and this same button confirms that version (Section 7.1).
• Clicking Confirm with an invalid form is blocked with the warning “Please fix the highlighted fields before confirming.” Additional confirm gate: both dates filled (ASSUMED — Q-8) and Total Value > 0 (ASSUMED — Q-4).
• First confirm dialog: “Confirm {MainOCNum}? A confirmed order can no longer be deleted (it can still be cancelled with a reason from the list).” Yes/No.
• Re-confirm dialog: title “Re-confirm Order”, text “Confirm the current changes to {MainOCNum}?”.
• On success: status becomes Confirmed, success toast “{MainOCNum} is now confirmed.”, header badge/title refresh, list reflects the change on return.

#### Alerts & messages (exact wording)

[TABLE 7: Table 7 · 20 rows · columns: # (text), Trigger (text), Kind (text), Title (text), Message (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Trigger | Kind | Title | Message |
| M-1 | List failed to load | Error toast | Load Failed | Could not load sales orders. |
| M-2 | Confirm from list (Saved row) | Confirm dialog | Confirm Order | Confirm {MainOCNum}? A confirmed order can no longer be deleted (it can still be cancelled with a reason from the list). |
| M-3 | Confirm succeeded | Success toast | Order Confirmed | {MainOCNum} is now confirmed. |
| M-4 | Confirm failed | Error toast | Confirm Failed | Could not confirm the order. |
| M-5 | Cancel dialog, blank reason | Warning toast | Validation | Reason is mandatory. |
| M-6 | Cancel succeeded | Success toast | Order Cancelled | {MainOCNum} was cancelled. |
| M-7 | Cancel failed | Error toast | Cancel Failed | Could not cancel the order. |
| M-8 | Delete on a non-deletable order | Warning toast | Not Allowed | {MainOCNum} is {Status} and cannot be deleted. Cancel it (with a reason) instead. |
| M-9 | Delete confirmation | Confirm dialog | Confirm Delete | Delete {MainOCNum}? This cannot be undone. |
| M-10 | Delete succeeded | Success toast | Order Deleted | {MainOCNum} was deleted. |
| M-11 | Delete failed | Error toast | Delete Failed | Could not delete the order. |
| M-12 | Bulk delete with blocked rows | Warning toast | Not Allowed | {n} of the selected order(s) are Confirmed or further along and cannot be deleted ({order list}). Deselect them and try again. |
| M-13 | Bulk delete confirmation | Confirm dialog | Confirm Delete | Delete {n} selected order(s)? This cannot be undone. |
| M-14 | Bulk delete succeeded | Success toast | Orders Deleted | {n} order(s) deleted. |
| M-15 | Bulk delete failed | Error toast | Delete Failed | Could not delete one or more orders. |
| M-16 | Detail: unknown id | Error toast | Not Found | That sales order does not exist. |
| M-17 | Detail failed to load | Error toast | Load Failed | Could not load the sales order. |
| M-18 | Auto-save failed | Error toast | Save Failed | Could not save the sales order. |
| M-19 | Confirm with invalid form | Warning toast | Validation | Please fix the highlighted fields before confirming. |
| M-20 | Re-confirm dialog | Confirm dialog | Re-confirm Order | Confirm the current changes to {MainOCNum}? |
Note: the mock’s list-side confirm dialog says a confirmed order “becomes read-only” — that contradicts the actual rule (confirmed orders remain editable through background versions). The real build must use the M-2 wording above on both screens. Flagged in Section 7.2.

## Workflow & status lifecycle

[TABLE 8: Table 8 · 6 rows · columns: Status (text), Badge severity (text), Meaning (text) · identifiers: Status]
| Status | Badge severity | Meaning |
| Saved | Draft (grey) | Auto-saved draft; fully editable; deletable. |
| Confirmed | Success (green) | Commercially confirmed; not deletable; edits create a new background version (Section 7.1). |
| Part Ship | Warning (amber) | Partially shipped — set by the shipment module, not by these screens. |
| Shipped | Success (green) | Fully shipped — set by the shipment module. |
| Closed | See Q-21 | Commercially closed — set downstream. |
| Cancelled | Error (red) | Cancelled with a mandatory reason; terminal. |

### Allowed transitions

[TABLE 9: Table 9 · 6 rows · columns: # (text), Transition (text), Trigger (text), Who / where (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Transition | Trigger | Who / where |
| T-1 | (new) → Saved | Automatic: all seed fields filled → record inserted | Auto-save engine, detail screen |
| T-2 | Saved → Confirmed | Manual Confirm + confirmation dialog (M-2) | Detail toolbar button; list context menu (Saved rows) |
| T-3 | Confirmed → Confirmed (new version) | Edit then manual Re-confirm (M-20) | Detail screen; real app versions in the background (7.1) |
| T-4 | Saved / Confirmed → Cancelled | Manual Cancel + mandatory reason (3.1.6). Mock also allows cancelling Part Ship / Shipped — ASSUMED excluded, Q-12 | List context menu |
| T-5 | Confirmed → Part Ship → Shipped → Closed | Shipment / closure documents in downstream modules | Out of scope for these screens (7.1) |
| T-6 | Saved → (deleted) | Manual Delete + confirmation (M-9). Mock also deletes Cancelled — ASSUMED excluded, Q-15 | List context menu / bulk bar |
• Cancelled and Closed are terminal: no cancel, no confirm, no reopen (ASSUMED — Q-14).
• Nothing that is Confirmed or further along may ever be hard-deleted.
• Irreversible actions (Delete, Cancel, Confirm) always use a confirmation dialog that spells out the impact.

## Validations master list
One line per field — its checks combined; shared rules are defined once under Conventions. Every rule is testable as written. Inline messages show at the field; toasts per Section 3.2.6.

[TABLE 10: Table 10 · 14 rows · columns: # (text), Rule (testable statement) (text), Where enforced (text), Message (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Rule (testable statement) | Where enforced | Message |
| V-1 | Ship Under PO Ref — required (seed); trimmed, not blank; ≤ 100 chars (input hard-stops at 100); unique per buyer (ASSUMED — Q-6, async check on blur). | Detail form + server | Ship Under PO Ref is required / cannot be blank |
| V-2 | Buyer — required (seed). | Detail form + server | Buyer is required |
| V-3 | Category — required (seed). | Detail form + server | Category is required |
| V-4 | Currency — required (seed). | Detail form + server | Currency is required |
| V-5 | Manager — ≤ 100 chars. | Detail form + server | — |
| V-6 | Total Quantity — required (seed); whole number; 1–1,000,000. | Detail form + server | Total Quantity is required / must be at least 1 / cannot exceed 1,000,000 |
| V-7 | Total Value — required (seed); Money (see Conventions); ≤ 99,999,999; must be > 0 to Confirm (ASSUMED — Q-4). | Detail form + server | Total Value is required / cannot be negative / cannot exceed 99,999,999 |
| V-8 | Delivery Date — required; on or after Order Initiation Date, re-validated whenever either date changes; both dates required before Confirm (ASSUMED — Q-8). | Detail form + server | Delivery Date cannot be earlier than the Order Initiation Date |
| V-9 | Fabric Instruction — ≤ 1000 chars. | Detail form + server | — |
| V-10 | Packing Instruction — ≤ 1000 chars. | Detail form + server | — |
| V-11 | Cancel reason — required, not blank (after trim). | Cancel dialog + server | Reason is mandatory. |
| V-12 | Confirm is blocked while any field is invalid. | Detail + server | Please fix the highlighted fields before confirming. |
| V-13 | Delete is allowed only for Saved orders (real rule — ASSUMED, Q-15; mock also allows Cancelled). Server re-validates. | List + server | M-8 |
| V-14 | A new order is created only after ALL seed fields (V-1, V-2, V-4, V-6, V-7) are filled and valid. | Auto-save engine | — |

## Out-of-scope & deltas

### Mock shortcuts — full real behaviour required
The mock simplified reality in the following places. The real build must implement the FULL behaviour in the right-hand column; none of these shortcuts may silently become the product.

[TABLE 11: Table 11 · 12 rows · columns: # (text), Mock shortcut (text), Required real behaviour (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Mock shortcut | Required real behaviour |
| D-1 | No versioning behind Confirm: confirmed orders are edited in place; the Confirm button simply re-saves. | Editing a Confirmed order spawns a new background version in Saved status; edits auto-save into that version; Confirm publishes it. The list keeps showing the last confirmed data, with a star flag when an edited-but-unconfirmed version exists. Full revision history retained. |
| D-2 | Client-side grid: all rows loaded once; filters, sort and paging run in the browser. | Server-side row model: paging, sorting, filtering and quick search executed by the API; set-filter values from the DDL API (ASSUMED — Q-18). |
| D-3 | Static dropdown lists (3 buyers, 4 categories, 3 seasons, 4 currencies) hardcoded in the component. | All selects fed from DDL APIs; inactive/archived options hidden for new entry but still displayed on historical orders (QA checklist §1). |
| D-4 | Manager is a free-text box. | Manager selected from the user/merchandiser directory (ASSUMED — Q-11). |
| D-5 | Order number: client-side placeholder “OC-DRAFT-nnnnnn” generated at first save. | Server-assigned sequential order number at insert (ASSUMED — Q-7); the client never invents order numbers. |
| D-6 | Auto-save PUTs the entire record on every change. | Auto-save PATCHes only dirty fields; concurrency handled per Q-20 (optimistic version check, conflict toast). |
| D-7 | No permissions: every user sees every action. | Role-based permissions on create / edit / Confirm / Cancel / Delete (ASSUMED — Q-16); unauthorized actions hidden or disabled with a tooltip. |
| D-8 | Statuses Part Ship / Shipped / Closed exist only as filter values; nothing transitions into them. | Set exclusively by the shipment/closure modules (T-5). These screens only display them. |
| D-9 | No order lines: single header-level TotalQty / TotalValue. | Article / size / colourway lines with matrix totals are a separate phase (Q-23); until then header totals are manual entries. |
| D-10 | Mock data-source fly-out widget (Team Data / Practice Copy / Start Empty) floats over every screen. | Studio-only tooling — must NOT be promoted into wfx-erp. |
| D-11 | No audit trail on any action. | Confirm, Cancel (with reason), Delete and every field change logged with user + timestamp, per ERP audit standards. |
| D-12 | Back-navigation loses list state. | List restores search, filters, sort and page on return from the detail screen. |

### Findings — mock defects and standards violations (do NOT implement)
Per the studio rule, standard violations found in the mock are flagged here instead of being specified. The spec text above already states the corrected behaviour.

[TABLE 12: Table 12 · 11 rows · columns: # (text), Type (text), Screen / area (text), Finding (verified in code) (text), Corrected rule in this spec (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Type | Screen / area | Finding (verified in code) | Corrected rule in this spec |
| F-1 — FIXED in the mock | Bug | List — Delivery Date, Created On columns | Columns inherited the default text filter while displaying formatted dates, so the floating filter matched the raw ISO string (e.g. “2026-09-15T00:00:00Z”) and filtering by what the user sees (“15 Sep”) failed. Both now declare cellDataType: 'dateString' + filter: 'agDateColumnFilter'; wfx-grid supplies ISO parsing, inclusive ranges and calendar-day comparison generically. | Date columns use the date column filter (3.1.3) — equals / before / after / from–to on a calendar picker. Build the real screen this way; a text filter on a date offers only “contains / begins with”, which cannot express “before this date” or a from–to range. |
| F-2 | Bug | List — Cancel flow | Cancelling saves the reason INTO the Comments field, overwriting any existing comments. | Dedicated CancelReason field + audit; Comments untouched (3.1.6, Q-13). |
| F-3 | Formatting gap | List & Detail — Total Qty | Quantity is displayed without a UOM anywhere. | Quantity always shown with its UOM (3.1.3, Q-1). |
| F-4 — PARTLY FIXED | Formatting inconsistency | List vs Detail — Total Value | Fixed: the list formatted value with 0 decimals (“$96,000”) while the detail input accepted 2 — same measure, two precisions; the list now shows 2 decimals everywhere (“$96,000.00”), matching the detail and Q-2. Still open: the locale is hardcoded to en-US for both value and quantity formatting, so thousand separators ignore the user’s locale. | 2 decimals everywhere, symbol + code, user-locale number formatting (3.1.3, Q-2/Q-3). The decimals half is done; the real build must still drop the hardcoded locale (Q-3). |
| F-5 | Wording | List — confirm dialog | Dialog says a confirmed order “becomes read-only”, contradicting the versioned-edit rule and the detail screen’s own wording. | Unified M-2 wording (3.2.6). |
| F-6 | Standards gap | List — row actions | No pinned-right actions column; actions reachable only via right-click context menu. | Pinned-right actions column plus the context menu (3.1.3). |
| F-7 | UX | List — quick search | Search fires on every keystroke with no debounce. | Debounced 300 ms (3.1.2, Q-17). |
| F-8 | Question | List — Status badge | Closed and Cancelled share the error (red) severity; Closed is a normal completion. | Severity decision pending Q-21. |
| F-9 | Consistency | List vs Detail — Confirm availability | List context menu offers Confirm only for Saved rows; the detail screen offers Confirm/Re-confirm for any loaded record. | Intentional per studio standards (detail carries re-confirm); list stays Saved-only. Documented in 3.1.4/3.2.5. |
| F-10 | Minor | Detail — Total Quantity input | Input widget allows typing 0 (widget min 0) while the rule requires ≥ 1; error only appears via form validation. | V-6 stands; input may keep soft min 0 with inline error. |
| F-11 | Minor | List — Cancel dialog | Dialog text does not name the order being cancelled. | Dialog must name the order (3.1.6). |

## Open questions
The product team was not available to answer the pre-finalization question batch, so every question below carries the proposed default, which this spec ADOPTS AS ASSUMED. Each assumption is marked “ASSUMED” where it is used in the body. Owner for every item: Product team (Sales) — confirmation required before development sign-off; any changed answer amends the referenced sections.

[TABLE 13: Table 13 · 24 rows · columns: # (text), Question (text), Adopted default (ASSUMED) (text), Used in (text) · identifiers: #]
| # | Question | Adopted default (ASSUMED) | Used in |
| Q-1 | Total Quantity has no UOM anywhere. Which UOM applies and where is it shown? | Order-level UOM field defaulting to “pcs”; quantity always displayed as “4,800 pcs” in list and detail. | 3.1.3, 3.2.2, F-3 |
| Q-2 | Value decimals differ between list (0 dp) and detail (2 dp). What is the display rule? | Always 2 decimals with currency symbol and code, identical in list, detail and documents; round half-up. | 3.1.3, V-7, F-4 |
| Q-3 | Are number formats (thousand separators) locale-fixed or per user? | User-locale formatting via the app-wide number formatting service; never a hardcoded locale. | F-4 |
| Q-4 | May Total Value be 0? | 0 allowed while Saved (draft); must be > 0 to Confirm. | V-7, 3.2.5 |
| Q-5 | Are the quantity bounds (integer, 1–1,000,000) and value bound (≤ 99,999,999) correct? | Yes — as mocked. | V-6…V-7 |
| Q-6 | Must Ship Under PO Ref be unique? | Unique per buyer; blocking inline error on save. | V-1 |
| Q-7 | How is the order number (MainOCNum) generated? | Server sequence “OC-{yyyy}-{seq}” assigned at first insert; never client-generated. | D-5, 3.2.3 |
| Q-8 | Are Order Initiation Date and Delivery Date mandatory? | Optional while Saved; both mandatory to Confirm. | V-8, 3.2.5 |
| Q-9 | Any absolute min/max on the dates (past/future)? | No absolute bounds (backdated orders exist); only the cross-field rule V-8, re-validated when either date changes. | V-8 |
| Q-10 | Season is optional in the mock — intentional? | Yes, optional and clearable. | 3.2.2 |
| Q-11 | Is Manager free text or a user list? | Selected from the user/merchandiser directory in the real app. | D-4 |
| Q-12 | Which statuses can be cancelled? The mock allows everything except Cancelled/Closed, including Part Ship and Shipped. | Saved and Confirmed only; partially/fully shipped orders follow an operations review outside this screen. | T-4, 3.1.4 |
| Q-13 | Where is the cancel reason stored, and what is its max length? | New CancelReason field, max 500 characters, audit-logged with user and timestamp; Comments never touched. | F-2, 3.1.6 |
| Q-13a | Comments has no max length in the mock. Limit? | 4000 characters. | 3.2.2 |
| Q-14 | Can a Cancelled order be reopened? | No — Cancelled is terminal; a replacement order is keyed fresh. | Section 4 |
| Q-15 | The mock allows deleting Cancelled orders. Correct? | No — only Saved orders are deletable; Cancelled orders are kept for audit. | V-13, T-6 |
| Q-16 | Who may Confirm / Cancel / Delete (roles)? | Standard WFX role permissions: merchandisers create/edit; managers confirm and cancel; delete restricted to managers. | D-7 |
| Q-17 | Quick-search scope and debounce? | Order No, Buyer name and PO Ref; 300 ms debounce. | 3.1.2, F-7 |
| Q-18 | Client-side grid: when does server paging arrive, page sizes, default sort? | Server-side row model from day one; page sizes 20/50/100 (default 20); default sort Created On descending. | D-2, 3.1.3 |
| Q-19 | Over-ship tolerance % and Part Ship/Shipped mechanics? | Owned by the shipment module; out of scope for these screens. | T-5, D-8 |
| Q-20 | Two users edit the same order — what happens? | Optimistic concurrency (row version); the later save gets a conflict error toast and a reload prompt. | D-6 |
| Q-21 | Closed shares the red badge with Cancelled. Correct severity? | Closed uses a neutral/secondary badge; red is reserved for Cancelled. | F-8, Section 4 |
| Q-22 | Empty-list experience? | “No sales orders found” overlay plus an Add New Order call to action. | 3.1.7 |
| Q-23 | When do article / size / colourway order lines arrive? | Separate phase after this header-level screen ships; header totals stay manual until then. | D-9 |

## Technical appendix — Data & API contract provisional
The committed mock JSON (mock-data/wfx-erp-product-sales-orders.mock.json) is the draft API contract. Field names are PascalCase DTO names matching the real xtOCMain response. The real backend must be reconciled field-by-field against this table during promotion.

[TABLE 14: Table 14 · 21 rows · columns: Field (text), Type (text), Example (text), Read by (text), Written by (text) · identifiers: Field]
| Field | Type | Example | Read by | Written by |
| id | string (UUID) | 6f9d3b2a-… | Both screens (row id, routing) | Server on insert (mock: client UUID) |
| MainOCID | number (xtOCMain PK) | 100001 | — (carried for the real API) | Server |
| MainOCNum | string | OC-2026-0001 | List (Order column), Detail (title), all messages | Server-generated sequence (Q-7) |
| ShipUnderPORef | string (≤100) | PO-ACME-5521 | List (Order column, secondary) | Detail (seed field) |
| BuyerCompanyCode | string | BUY001 | List (Buyer secondary) | Detail (Buyer select value) |
| BuyerCompanyName | string | Acme Retail Group | List (Buyer primary), search | Derived from Buyer selection |
| ProductCatCode | string | APPAREL | List (Category) | Detail (Category select) |
| Season | string | SS26 | List (Season) | Detail (Order Season select; optional) |
| CurrencyCode | string (ISO 4217) | USD | List (Total Value formatting), Detail | Detail (Currency select; seed) |
| ManagerName | string (≤100) | Priya Nair | List (Manager) | Detail |
| Status | enum: Saved | Confirmed | Part Ship | Shipped | Closed | Cancelled | Saved | List (badge, filters), Detail (Confirm logic) | Lifecycle actions only — never a free edit |
| TotalQty | integer (1–1,000,000) | 4800 | List (Total Qty) | Detail (seed field) |
| TotalValue | decimal(2) (0–99,999,999) | 96000 | List (Total Value) | Detail (seed field) |
| OrderInitiationDate | ISO 8601 datetime, date-only meaning | 2026-06-10T00:00:00Z | Detail | Detail (datepicker) |
| DeliveryDate | ISO 8601 datetime; ≥ OrderInitiationDate | 2026-09-15T00:00:00Z | List (Delivery Date), Detail | Detail (datepicker) |
| CreatedBy | string (≤100) | Ayesha Khan | List (Created By, avatar + name) | Server on insert — the authenticated user; never client-supplied |
| CreatedOn | ISO 8601 datetime | 2026-06-12T09:30:00Z | List (Created On, default sort) | Server on insert |
| FabricInstruction | string (≤1000) | 100% combed cotton… | Detail (Instruction tab) | Detail |
| PackingInstruction | string (≤1000) | Solid color solid size… | Detail (Instruction tab) | Detail |
| Comments | string | Priority order… | Detail (Instruction tab) | Detail ONLY — never the cancel flow (7.2) |
| CancelReason (NEW) | string (≤500, ASSUMED) | — | Audit / future display | Cancel dialog (Q-13) |

### Service surface (real WfxSalesOrderApiService)

[TABLE 15: Table 15 · 6 rows · columns: Method (mock today) (text), Real endpoint (to define) (text), Notes (text)]
| Method (mock today) | Real endpoint (to define) | Notes |
| fetchOrders(): Observable<IWfxSalesOrderListItem[]> | GET /sales-orders (server-side paging/sort/filter params) | One call per grid block; no N+1. |
| getOrder(id) | GET /sales-orders/{id} | 404 → M-16 flow. |
| saveOrder(order) | POST /sales-orders (insert on seed completion); PATCH /sales-orders/{id} (dirty fields only) | Mock PUTs the whole record — real build patches per field (7.1). |
| deleteOrder(id) | DELETE /sales-orders/{id} | Server re-validates the delete rule (never trust the client). |
| — (new) | POST /sales-orders/{id}/confirm | Creates/publishes the confirmed version; server re-validates. |
| — (new) | POST /sales-orders/{id}/cancel { reason } | Server enforces mandatory reason and allowed statuses. |
• All list/detail reads and writes go through one thin per-feature service; components never call HTTP directly.
• Server is the source of truth for every rule in Section 6 — client validation is a convenience, not the enforcement.

CANDIDATES FOR REVIEW (possible definitions, formulas, validations, steps; not confirmed knowledge)
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Overview): The mock is intentionally lenient; this specification is not — it is the contract the development team builds from, and it goes to QA and then to live production.
- workflow_steps (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Overview › Who uses it2): Who uses it2: / 1. Merchandisers / sales coordinators — create and maintain orders, enter instructions. / 2. Sales managers — review and Confirm orders, cancel with a reason. / 3. Downstream teams (planning, production, shipping) — read confirmed order data; they do not edit here.
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Overview › Where it sits in the ERP): It is the upstream source for production planning, BOM and shipment documents; statuses beyond Confirmed (Part Ship, Shipped, Closed) are driven by those downstream modules, not by these two screens.
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Overview › Where it sits in the ERP): Order line items (article / size / colourway breakdowns) are not part of the mock and are out of scope (see Section 7).
- table (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen inventory & navigation flow, table 1): Table 1: #, Screen, Route, Purpose (3 rows)
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): Any pending auto-save is flushed before navigating away; the flush must complete (or fail with an error toast) — a navigation must never silently drop an unsaved change.
- validation (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): Any pending auto-save is flushed before navigating away; the flush must complete (or fail with an error toast) — a navigation must never silently drop an unsaved change.
- workflow_steps (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): Navigation rules: / 1. List → Detail (edit): click the order-number link in the Order column, or right-click a row and choose Edit. Both open /sales/orders/{id}. / 2. List → Detail (new): the “+ Add New Order” button in the page toolbar opens /sales/orders/new. / 3. Detail → List: the back arrow in the page header returns to /sales/orders. Any pending auto-save is flushed before navigating away; the flush must complete (or fail with an error toast) — a navigation must never silently drop an unsaved change. / 4. Unknown order id: an error toast “That sales order does not exist.” is shown and the user is returned to the list. / 5. Browser/page titles: “Sales Orders” (list), “New Sales Order” (new), “Sales Order” (edit).
- validation (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen inventory & navigation flow › Navigation rules): The real screen must restore the list exactly as the user left it — search text, status filter, column filters, sort and page (QA checklist §5).
- table (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Conventions, table 2): Table 2: Convention, Definition (5 rows; identifiers: Convention)
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order List (S-1) › Layout): Floating selection bar appears when one or more rows are selected, with the selection count, a Clear action, and a Delete action.
- workflow_steps (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order List (S-1) › Layout): Layout: / 1. Page header: breadcrumb “Sales”, title “Sales Orders”, subtitle, and a primary “+ Add New Order” button. / 2. Content toolbar: quick-search input (“Search by order no. or buyer”) and a clearable, searchable Status dropdown. / 3. Grid inside a surface card; floating filter row pinned under the headers; pagination footer always visible (never covered by other UI). / 4. Floating selection bar appears when one or more rows are selected, with the selection count, a Clear action, and a Delete action.
- workflow_steps (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order List (S-1) › Toolbar behaviours): Toolbar behaviours: / 1. Quick search matches Order No (MainOCNum) OR Buyer name, case-insensitive substring, trimmed. Real build: debounce 300 ms and extend to PO Ref (ASSUMED — Q-17). / 2. Status dropdown filters to exactly one status; clearable (shows all). Values: Saved, Confirmed, Part Ship, Shipped, Closed, Cancelled. / 3. Toolbar filters and in-grid column filters combine (logical AND).

Default column config: resizable, sortable, floating filter row on, min width 90. / 2. Set-filter values: fed from the DDL API in the real app (mock auto-derives from row data). / 3. Pagination: page sizes 20 / 50 / 100, default 20. Default sort: Created On descending (ASSUMED — Q-18). / 4. Row model: the mock grid is client-side. Actions column: the mock exposes row actions only through the right-click context menu. After a successful bulk delete the selection is cleared and the list reloads.

Modal, header “Cancel Order”, helper text “Enter a reason to cancel this order.”, one required Reason textarea (4 rows), buttons OK (primary) / Close. / 2. OK with a blank/whitespace reason shows the warning “Reason is mandatory.” and keeps the dialog open. / 3. OK with a reason sets Status = Cancelled and stores the reason. The real build stores it in a dedicated CancelReason field with an audit entry (who/when); it must NOT overwrite the order’s Comments as the mock does — flagged, Section 7.2 (ASSUMED — Q-13). / 4. Close / X dismisses without changes. / 5. Real build addition: the dialog must name the order being cancelled (e.g. “Cancel OC-2026-0001”) — the mock text is generic.
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3)): There is NO Save button — the screen auto-saves (see 3.2.3).
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3)): Confirm is the only manual action.

- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Auto-save behaviour): Seed fields (all must be filled before the record is created): Ship Under PO Ref, Buyer, Category, Currency, Total Quantity, Total Value.
- validation (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Auto-save behaviour): Seed fields (all must be filled before the record is created): Ship Under PO Ref, Buyer, Category, Currency, Total Quantity, Total Value.
- validation (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Auto-save behaviour): The server assigns the real order number at this insert (ASSUMED — Q-7); the mock’s client-side “OC-DRAFT-nnnnnn” placeholder must not ship.
- validation (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Auto-save behaviour): Loaded values never count as dirty — opening an order must not trigger a save.
- workflow_steps (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Auto-save behaviour): Auto-save behaviour: / 1. Seed fields (all must be filled before the record is created): Ship Under PO Ref, Buyer, Category, Currency, Total Quantity, Total Value. Season, dates and all Instruction-tab fields are NOT seed fields. / 2. New order: the record is inserted automatically the moment the last seed field is filled and valid. The server assigns the real order number at this insert (ASSUMED — Q-7); the mock’s client-side “OC-DRAFT-nnnnnn” placeholder must not ship. / 3. Existing order: every change is debounce-saved automatically. The mock PUTs the whole record; the real screen PATCHes only the dirty fields (Section 7.1). / 4. The save-status indicator in the toolbar shows idle → saving → saved / error. A failed save shows the toast “Save Failed — Could not save the sales order.” and the indicator stays in the error state until a subsequent save succeeds. / 5. Navigating back flushes any pending save first (see Section 2). / 6. Loaded values never count as dirty — opening an order must not trigger a save.
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Validation display): Errors appear inline per field once the field is touched, using the standard field-error styling; required fields carry the * marker.
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Validation display): Exact rule texts are in Section 6 (Validations master list).
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Confirm action): Confirm is visible for any existing (already auto-saved) record — including an already-Confirmed one.
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Confirm action): Re-confirm after an edit is deliberate: in the real app, editing a confirmed order creates a new background version in Saved status, and this same button confirms that version (Section 7.1).
- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Confirm action): Clicking Confirm with an invalid form is blocked with the warning “Please fix the highlighted fields before confirming.” Additional confirm gate: both dates filled (ASSUMED — Q-8) and Total Value > 0 (ASSUMED — Q-4).
- validation (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Confirm action): Clicking Confirm with an invalid form is blocked with the warning “Please fix the highlighted fields before confirming.” Additional confirm gate: both dates filled (ASSUMED — Q-8) and Total Value > 0 (ASSUMED — Q-4).
- workflow_steps (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Screen specifications › Sales Order Detail (S-2 / S-3) › Confirm action): Confirm action: / 1. Confirm is visible for any existing (already auto-saved) record — including an already-Confirmed one. Re-confirm after an edit is deliberate: in the real app, editing a confirmed order creates a new background version in Saved status, and this same button confirms that version (Section 7.1). / 2. Clicking Confirm with an invalid form is blocked with the warning “Please fix the highlighted fields before confirming.” Additional confirm gate: both dates filled (ASSUMED — Q-8) and Total Value > 0 (ASSUMED — Q-4). / 3. First confirm dialog: “Confirm {MainOCNum}? A confirmed order can no longer be deleted (it can still be cancelled with a reason from the list).” Yes/No. / 4. Re-confirm dialog: title “Re-confirm Order”, text “Confirm the current changes to {MainOCNum}?”. / 5. On success: status becomes Confirmed, success toast “{MainOCNum} is now confirmed.”, header badge/title refresh, list reflects the change on return.

- definition (§ Sales Orders — Product Mock Spec › Workflow & status lifecycle › Allowed transitions): Cancelled and Closed are terminal: no cancel, no confirm, no reopen (ASSUMED — Q-14).

Cancelled and Closed are terminal: no cancel, no confirm, no reopen (ASSUMED — Q-14). / 2. Nothing that is Confirmed or further along may ever be hard-deleted. / 3. Irreversible actions (Delete, Cancel, Confirm) always use a confirmation dialog that spells out the impact.
